items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: And, when I was in the band, the piano player was Elmer Schoble.

ctx.x: Because he and Wellstead worked a lot later. Yes. Right. Did Janice have any steady jobs in this period that you were with him?

Yes. Mostly at the Central Plaza. We used to work there every Friday and Saturday night. And we used to work a few other jobs too. We did, I don't know, we were on the Arthur Godfrey Show. A lot of things like that. Who else was in the band? A guy named Dick Smith on trumpet. He was from the west coast. He was influenced by Bunk mainly. And, well, before I was in the band, there was a clarinet player named Tom Sharpstein, who used to do a very good imitation of George Lewis. And, when I was in the band, the piano…

And, he certainly was pleased with the first New Orleans men to come up because he worked with them steadily. Both at the Friars and at Midway Gardens. Although, now that I say Midway, I can't remember that there were many New Orleans. They were mainly Chicagoans. However, they were greatly influenced by the Friars where Schoble had been active. Did Schoble continue his activity in composing or arranging at that time?
